blocks.rationale: Create the requested two-stage legal graph for disclosure questions. The preliminary helper determines whether the query's recipient category reaches Paragraph 4(a)'s representative exception, including the existential overlap between “professional advisors” and the expressly permitted legal or financial advisors. The terminal then applies Paragraph 3(c)'s general prohibition subject to that exception. This directly targets the failed nda-7 view while also handling nda-5.

skill.intent: Determine whether a disclosure-permission query identifies at least one recipient category covered by the contractual Representatives exception, subject to its stated confidentiality and need-to-know restrictions.

inputs.name: current_question
inputs.question: What is the caller-supplied disclosure-permission question whose stated recipient category must be tested against the Representatives exception?

outputs.name: exception_applies
outputs.description: Whether the query identifies at least one category within the Paragraph 4(a) Representatives permission and the source supplies its confidentiality, need-to-know, and Business Purpose limitations.

premises.name: permitted_representative_classes
premises.question: Which recipient classes does Paragraph 4(a) expressly include as Representatives?

origin.quote: each Party may disclose the other Party’s Confidential Information to its directors, officers, employees, legal advisors, financial advisors and accountants

premises.name: representatives_must_be_confidentiality_bound
premises.question: Does Paragraph 4(a) require permitted Representatives to be bound by consistent confidentiality obligations?

origin.quote: each bound by obligations of confidentiality consistent with this Agreement

premises.name: representatives_must_have_bona_fide_need_to_know
premises.question: Does Paragraph 4(a) restrict permitted Representatives to those with a bona fide need to know?

origin.quote: who have a bona fide need to know (“Representatives”)

premises.name: disclosure_limited_to_business_purpose
premises.question: Does Paragraph 4(a) limit representative disclosure to what is necessary for the Business Purpose?

origin.quote: but only to the extent necessary to carry out the Business Purpose

source_obligations.statement: Check whether the disclosure query reaches an expressly listed Representative category, including a professional-advisor category containing the listed legal or financial advisors, while preserving Paragraph 4(a)'s confidentiality, need-to-know, and Business Purpose restrictions.

origin.quote: each Party may disclose the other Party’s Confidential Information to its directors, officers, employees, legal advisors, financial advisors and accountants, each bound by obligations of confidentiality consistent with this Agreement, who have a bona fide need to know (“Representatives”), but only to the extent necessary to carry out the Business Purpose

source_provenance.quote: each Party may disclose the other Party’s Confidential Information to its directors, officers, employees, legal advisors, financial advisors and accountants, each bound by obligations of confidentiality consistent with this Agreement, who have a bona fide need to know (“Representatives”), but only to the extent necessary to carry out the Business Purpose

skill.intent: Classify a Receiving Party disclosure-permission query by applying the general third-party prohibition together with Paragraph 4's computed Representatives exception.

inputs.name: current_question
inputs.question: What is the caller-supplied native disclosure-permission question to classify?

inputs.name: representative_exception_applies
inputs.question: Does Paragraph 4(a)'s Representatives exception apply to at least one recipient category stated in this disclosure query?

outputs.name: answer
outputs.description: Native ContractNLI classification of the disclosure-permission statement.

premises.name: general_third_party_nondisclosure_rule
premises.question: Does Paragraph 3(c) generally prohibit disclosure of Confidential Information to third parties without prior written consent?

origin.quote: not to disclose such Confidential Information to third parties (including, without limitation, any clients, affiliates, independent contractors and consultants) without the prior, written consent of the Disclosing Party

premises.name: prohibition_expressly_subject_to_paragraph4
premises.question: Does Paragraph 3(c) expressly make its prohibition subject to disclosures permitted under Paragraph 4?

origin.quote: except as expressly permitted under Paragraph 4

source_obligations.statement: Treat the general third-party nondisclosure obligation as controlling unless the separately computed Paragraph 4 Representatives exception applies; when it applies, the queried permission is entailed rather than contradicted.
